run_note: Heads up: today's update only covers 12 of the usual 14 holdings. L3Harris Technologies and Microsoft weren't scored because of a technical problem on our side — nothing to do with the companies themselves.

LHX.sentence: L3Harris Technologies didn't get scored in today's run because of a technical problem on our side — nothing happened to the company itself. It should be back in tomorrow's update.

ASML.sentence: ASML drifted down again and is now about 12% off its high, which is just a cooling-off spell — they're still the only company on earth that makes the machines needed to print the most advanced chips.

LIN.sentence: Linde had a quiet, slightly-up week — they supply oxygen, nitrogen and other gases on long contracts and nudge prices up a little each quarter, which really is the whole story with this one.

MSFT.sentence: Microsoft didn't get scored in today's run because of a technical problem on our side — nothing happened to the company itself. It should be back in tomorrow's update.

TMO.sentence: Thermo Fisher slipped a bit, and the thing to watch is their lab-supplies business, which is still near the bottom of its cycle — the hope is that demand picks back up over the coming year.

CVX.sentence: Chevron fell a few percent as oil eased, but remember today's profits are puffed up by Middle East fighting pushing oil prices well above normal — so moves up and down are mostly the oil price swinging, not the company itself changing.

NOW.sentence: ServiceNow has fallen a long way from its high even though its business of automating corporate and government paperwork — increasingly with AI assistants — is still healthy, which is why it looks unusually beaten-down for such a steady performer.

GLNCY.sentence: Glencore dropped even as copper prices climbed, an odd gap for a miner that digs copper and cobalt — history suggests the share price eventually catches up to where the metal is trading.

MLM.sentence: Martin Marietta rose after a good update — the price it gets per ton of crushed stone is still climbing nicely, which matters more than the headline figures, since each quarry effectively owns its own patch of the map.

KOF.sentence: Coca-Cola FEMSA edged up, though a weakening Mexican peso works against it since most of its earnings come in pesos that convert into fewer dollars.

UBER.sentence: Uber climbed again and people keep booking a lot more rides and food orders than a year ago — the big open question is still whether self-driving-car companies put their cars on Uber's app or run their own.

AMKBY.sentence: Maersk, the Danish container-shipping giant, slipped a touch, and its shares are priced well below the value of its own fleet of ships — a quiet reflection of a sluggish stretch for global trade.

MA.sentence: Mastercard jumped over 3% and is priced almost in line with Visa right now; people keep tapping their cards more than ever, so there's no crack in the business, just normal day-to-day movement.

ISRG.sentence: The surgical-robot maker edged up, and there's a real gap here — hospitals are expected to keep doing well over 10% more operations with its machines, yet the stock still sits far below its high.
